blindSummary:
This is a calm, safe destination for transgender visitors. It was one of the first countries in the world to introduce legal gender recognition by self-declaration — the 2015 gender-recognition act lets adults change their legal gender without medical requirements — and bathroom use is unrestricted. A hate-crime law covering sexual orientation and gender identity finally took effect at the end of 2024, equality law bans discrimination in employment, housing and services, and marriage equality was approved by referendum in 2015.

The caveats are stagnation and a mildly worsening climate rather than active rollback. The 2015 law is binary-only and long-promised reform (non-binary, under-16s) has stalled; transphobic hate speech remains uncriminalised after a 2024 government U-turn; a 2025 university study documented rising discrimination against sexual and gender minorities; and total hate-crime reports rose about 15% in 2025 (racism and xenophobia are the most common motives). None of this amounts to criminal exposure or physical danger for a visitor.

Day-to-day, the country is welcoming with low violent crime and a strong civil-society support network.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory exists; general urban crime is low.
blindSourceSummaries: Foreign broadsheet (Dec 2025): this country's gender-recognition decade - reflections on the 2015 gender-recognition act, seen as a move away from the country's dominant-church past; first-person accounts of what self-declaration meant.
Official text of the 2015 gender-recognition act (national statute database, updated to 2026): enables legal gender recognition by self-declaration.

LGBTQ+ youth organisation: the country now has a hate-crime law - the criminal-justice hate-offences act 2024 came into force in December 2024, meaning crimes motivated by LGBTQ+ identity carry enhanced punishment.
National police hate-crime statistics page (2025): police-recorded hate-crime data for this country.
National daily (Aug 2026): reports of hate crimes up 15% in 2025, with racism and xenophobia the most common motives - official police data.
National daily (July 2025): a national-university study finds discrimination against sexual and gender minorities here has increased.

Trans community network (July 2025): 10 years on, trans activists reflect on the gender-recognition act - this country is one of only 11 countries in its region offering gender recognition through self-determination (no psychological or medical evaluation); 35 countries in the region still require a diagnosis, and some require sterilisation; renewed calls to address gaps in trans rights and healthcare.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): marriage equality by popular vote 2015; joint adoption; self-determination-based gender markers; the equality acts ban discrimination on 'gender' but do not explicitly cover gender identity/expression/sex characteristics (though interpreted to protect trans people under 'gender'); intersex people remain among the least protected, with nonconsensual surgeries reported in 2025.

Crowd-sourced safety data: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change legal with no restrictions; gender-affirming care legal but restricted for minors; no nonbinary recognition; hate-crime protections cover SOGI; employment/housing discrimination protections cover sexual orientation only; intersex infant surgery not banned; conversion therapy not banned. High public support (61% support LGBT openness, fourth of 26 surveyed regions).

Migrant-rights organisation's guide (with a national trans organisation and a national LGBT organisation) for LGBTQI+ citizens of this country returning home: rights, inclusive services, community reconnection - practical returnee information.

Investigative news site (April 2025): barriers to accessing transgender healthcare - almost 20 trans adults describe traumatic experiences and long wait times at the national gender service; the health authority admitted trans healthcare is 'limited' and 'not meeting people's full range of needs'.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 402 paywall); the underlying foreign-broadsheet article (Sept 2024) reports this country backing down on hate-speech laws amid the trans debate.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2015 gender-recognition act (binary-only, stalled non-binary/under-16 reform) is a resident-facing process.
